## Six steps

```{=html}
<section class="eday-step">
  <div class="num">1<small>~30 min</small></div>
  <div>
    <h3>💎 Drill the dates and frames cold</h3>
    <p>Open Memorize Now. Run the dates drill twice in a row. Then the frames drill twice. Goal: 9 of 10 dates and all 4 frames in your fingers without thinking.</p>
    <div class="actions"><a href="memorize.html" class="primary">Open Memorize Now</a></div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="eday-step">
  <div class="num">2<small>~75 min</small></div>
  <div>
    <h3>📖 Walk through the eight stops</h3>
    <p>Read the Walkthrough end to end. Do the fill-ins in real time — they're not optional, they're how the spine gets into your head. Check the box at the bottom of each stop.</p>
    <div class="actions"><a href="walkthrough.html" class="primary">Open The Walkthrough</a></div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="eday-step">
  <div class="num">3<small>~25 min</small></div>
  <div>
    <h3>📝 Outline one essay from memory</h3>
    <p>Pick any of the 17 questions on the Framework. Outline it on paper using the five-paragraph spine: thesis · three moves · counter · tie-back. Don't read the model first.</p>
    <div class="actions"><a href="index.html">Pick a question</a><a href="sample-answers.html">Compare to model after</a></div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="eday-step">
  <div class="num">4<small>~10 min</small></div>
  <div>
    <h3>🧠 Read the Cram Sheet once, slowly</h3>
    <p>Last pass over the dates table, the four frames, the three throughlines, and the five thesis statements. If a date doesn't have an image in your head, pause and rebuild it from the Memorize page.</p>
    <div class="actions"><a href="cram-sheet.html">Open Cram Sheet</a></div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="eday-step">
  <div class="num">5<small>15 min</small></div>
  <div>
    <h3>🌬 Walk and breathe</h3>
    <p>Close the laptop. Take a real walk — outside, or up a stairwell — for fifteen minutes. No phone, no notes. The material is in. The walk lets it settle.</p>
    <div class="actions"><a href="../reset.html">Open Reset (if you'd rather sit)</a></div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="eday-step">
  <div class="num">6<small>5 min</small></div>
  <div>
    <h3>📋 The 30-minute spine, before you walk in</h3>
    <p>Right before the exam, glance through the spine below. Don't read anything new. Don't open Twitter. Drink water.</p>
  </div>
</section>
```

## The 30-minute spine

```{=html}
<section class="eday-spine">
  <h2>The five things you need cold</h2>
  <ol>
    <li><strong>Three throughlines:</strong> the API → Abraham Accords pivot · the Nash equilibrium carousel · Iran as the linkage engine.</li>
    <li><strong>Eight dates that prove you know the shape:</strong> 1948 (Nakba) · 1967 (Six-Day War + UNSC 242) · 1979 (Iranian Revolution) · 1982 (Hezbollah founded) · 1993 (Oslo) · 2002 (API, Beirut) · 2020 (Abraham Accords) · 8 December 2024 (Damascus falls).</li>
    <li><strong>Four frames you cite by author + year:</strong> Bellin (2004) · Brownlee, Masoud, Reynolds (2015) · Mitchell (2011) · Goodarzi (2006).</li>
    <li><strong>Four actors:</strong> Israel, Palestinians (Hamas + PA), Iran, Saudi/Gulf. The US is the structural backstop, not a fifth player.</li>
    <li><strong>One thesis sentence to adapt:</strong> <em>"In 2026, the regional order has shifted from API-anchored linkage to Abraham-Accords-style security-and-economics linkage, with Iran as the engine connecting both spheres until Damascus fell on 8 December 2024."</em></li>
  </ol>
</section>
```

## In the room

```{=html}
<div class="eday-mini">
  <div>
    <h4>Read first</h4>
    <ul>
      <li>Read every prompt before writing</li>
      <li>Pick the one you can outline cleanest</li>
      <li>Outline 5 min before writing</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div>
    <h4>Structure</h4>
    <ul>
      <li>Thesis sentence in P1</li>
      <li>Three moves in P2-4</li>
      <li>Counter + rebuttal in P5</li>
      <li>Tie-back in last sentence</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div>
    <h4>Density signals</h4>
    <ul>
      <li>Drop ≥4 specific dates per essay</li>
      <li>Cite ≥2 frames by author + year</li>
      <li>Name a throughline by name</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div>
    <h4>If stuck</h4>
    <ul>
      <li>Write "this question is really about ____"</li>
      <li>List 4 dates, 2 authors in margin</li>
      <li>Start the first paragraph before improving the plan</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
```

You have the spine. Walk in.
